The test image shows a corn leaf with extensive tan/brown necrotic tissue along both leaf margins in a wavy, irregular pattern, while the center remains green. There appear to be some dark streaks or spots within the lesion areas.

This is a **leaf** disease. Top candidates from the leaf classes: Goss_S_Wilt (wavy-edged lesions with freckles), Stewart_S_Disease (bleached streaks), Northern_Leaf_Blight (cigar-shaped lesions), Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Goss vs Stewart distinction is key.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with my top candidate.
Goss's Wilt reference shows similar extensive necrosis with wavy edges progressing from margins. Let me check Stewart's Disease next.
Stewart's shows more linear, bleached streaks along veins. The test image has more margin-focused, wavy necrosis. Let me check Northern Leaf Blight.
NLB shows distinct cigar-shaped lesions, not matching the margin necrosis pattern. Let me check Anthracnose.
Anthracnose shows smaller, discrete lesions with dark margins on the leaf edge, not the extensive margin necrosis seen in the test image. Let me check Southern Corn Leaf Blight next.
SCLB shows small rectangular lesions, very different. Let me check Gray Leaf Spot.
Gray Leaf Spot shows narrow rectangular lesions bounded by veins, not matching. Let me check Maize Dwarf Mosaic Virus (for the possible streaking/mosaic pattern).
MDMV shows mosaic/mottling, very different. I've used 7 views across 7 classes. The test image most closely matches Goss's Wilt. Let me use my final view on another Goss's Wilt reference to confirm.

This second Goss's Wilt reference shows extensive bleaching/necrosis with dark freckle-like streaks and wavy margins, consistent with the disease pattern.

**Analysis summary:**
- The test image shows a corn leaf with extensive tan/brown necrotic tissue along both margins in a wavy, irregular pattern, with the center remaining green
- The necrosis has wavy edges characteristic of Goss's Wilt
- Dark spots/freckles appear within the necrotic areas
- The pattern matches Goss's Wilt references much better than any other candidate (Stewart's has more linear streaks, NLB has cigar-shaped lesions, GLS has rectangular vein-bounded lesions, SCLB has small scattered lesions, Anthracnose has discrete small lesions with dark margins, MDMV has mosaic patterns)
